name: Amber
description: Labdanum and vanilla, bergamot on top: the warm, sweet, resinous accord under a century of oriental perfumery.
lesson: An amber is built on a dark resin (labdanum) and vanilla sweetness (vanillin), often with a citrus top to lift it. Balance the two: too much labdanum turns leathery and dry, too much vanillin turns sugary.

name: Chypre
description: The chypre skeleton, made famous in 1917: bergamot over a base of labdanum, oakmoss and patchouli.
lesson: A chypre contrasts a bright citrus top with a dark, mossy, resinous base. Oakmoss is strictly limited for safety, so work it diluted and use only a little.

name: Fougère
description: The fougère ('fern'), born in 1882 with the first perfume built on synthetic coumarin: lavender, coumarin, oakmoss and bergamot.
lesson: A fougère sets fresh lavender over the sweet hay of coumarin and a mossy base. Coumarin is powerful and limited for safety: a few parts is plenty.

name: Cologne
description: Mostly citrus with aromatic herbs and very little base: fresh, bright and short-lived.
lesson: An eau de cologne is mostly citrus with a few herbs and almost no base: fresh, generous and gone within a couple of hours.
